meta.title: Ban the box in state public hiring, starting law as of January 2025, 56 places
meta.status: PARTIAL: 52 of 56 places answered from fetched pages (NELP Oct 2021 guide, Collateral Consequences Resource Center 50-state comparison); Guam, American Samoa, the Northern Mariana Islands and the U.S. Virgin Islands NOT FOUND; no dated source for changes between Oct 2021 and Jan 2025; New Hampshire's sources conflict (see places). Nothing filled from memory.

places.quote: It has no law regulating consideration of conviction in public or private employment, except for a “certificate of employability”
Alaska has no general law regulating consideration of criminal record in employment or occupational licensing.

places.note: No source found covering American Samoa.

places.quote: prohibits certain state agencies from inquiring into an applicant’s conviction or arrest history until after submission of a job application and an initial interview
Arkansas has no fair employment law that would generally restrict how employers consider a conviction record
places.note: Not on NELP's 2021 list of 37 states; CCRC page does not mention application-stage inquiries for Arkansas; lower confidence.

places.citation: AB 218 (2013), Gov. Code 12952 via AB 1008 (2017); state-agency policy 2010
places.quote: requires public- and private-sector employers to delay any conviction background check as well as any questions about or consideration of a job applicant’s conviction history until after the employer extends a conditional offer
prohibits state agencies from performing a background check until the agency determines that the applicant is a finalist
places.note: State applications already omitted the question before 2012 (NELP commentary).

places.quote: prohibits any employer—public or private—from inquiring about arrest and conviction history information on an initial employment application
prohibits public employers from inquiring into or considering criminal or credit histories of an applicant until after the completion of the first interview

places.citation: Returning Citizens Public Employment Inclusion Act of 2010 (public, effective 2011); Fair Criminal Record Screening Amendment Act of 2014 (private)
places.quote: Returning Citizens Public Employment Inclusion Act of 2010, which went into effect in 2011 for public employers
Florida does not limit application-stage inquiries into criminal history
removed questions regarding criminal history from all applications for state employment

places.note: No source found covering Guam (CCRC and NELP 50-state sources omit it; search engines returned nothing).

places.quote: prohibits employers from inquiring into an applicant’s conviction history until after a conditional offer of employment has been made
Idaho has no law generally regulating consideration of criminal record in employment.

places.citation: Executive Order 1 (2013, Gov. Quinn) for state agencies; private: 820 ILCS 75 (2014)
places.quote: required the Illinois Bureau of Personnel … to modify the Application for State Employment (the “CMS100”) for all state employing agencies
requiring the removal of “questions regarding convictions and criminal history” on job applications for positions within the state’s executive branch
Until 2020, Iowa had no general laws limiting or regulating consideration of criminal history in employment or licensing
places.note: CCRC mentions no application-stage rule for Iowa after 2020 (licensing law only); NELP 2021 list omits Iowa.

places.quote: ensure that job applicants are not asked about their conviction or arrest records “during the initial stage of a state employment application”
removing “questions regarding convictions and criminal history” from applications for jobs within the state executive branch

places.citation: La. R.S. 42:1701 (HB 266 / Act 398, 2016); Civil Service Rule 22.4.1 (2017)
places.quote: prohibits many state government employers from inquiring into an applicant’s criminal history until after the applicant has been given an opportunity to interview
places.note: Private employers get a separate 2021 fair-chance law (La. R.S. 23:291.2) that is not a ban-the-box.

places.citation: Me. Rev. Stat. tit. 5, s.792 (LD 170, 2019); private/municipal: LD 1167 (2021)
places.quote: prohibiting questions about criminal history on applications for state government jobs

places.citation: Md. Code, State Pers. & Pens. s.2-203 (SB 4, 2013); private: Lab. & Empl. 3-1401 to -1405 (2020)
places.quote: prohibits state government employers from inquiring into the criminal history of an applicant for employment until the applicant has been provided an opportunity for an interview

places.citation: Mass. Gen. Laws ch.151B s.4(9 1/2) (St. 2010 c.256; amended St. 2018 c.69)
places.quote: employers are prohibited from using an initial written employment application to ask whether an applicant has been previously convicted
prohibits state departments and agencies from including questions about conviction or arrest history on job applications or job postings

places.citation: Minn. Stat. 364.021 (2009); extended to private by SF 523 (2013)
places.quote: adds section 364.021 to Minn. Stat. § 364 et seq. applying ban-the-box to public employment
none of the limits on application-stage inquiries for public employers that exist in numerous states
directing all departments, agencies and boards and commissions in the state’s executive branch to remove questions relating to an individual’s criminal history from initial employment applications
Montana has no law regulating consideration of criminal record in public or private employment, including the limits on application-stage inquiry by public employers
Public employers are prohibited from inquiring into a job applicant’s criminal history until after the employer has determined the applicant meets the minimum job requirements
an employer may not consider the particular criminal history of an applicant until after (1) the final in-person interview or (2) a conditional offer
prohibits state government employers from asking about arrest or conviction history on job applications, instead requiring them to wait until an interview
places.note: CONFLICT: CCRC's (2025) NH profile says there are 'no limits on application-stage inquiries'. NELP names HB 253; unresolved, verify against RSA text.

places.quote: public and private employers cannot inquire into a candidate’s criminal history until the employer has conducted the first interview
public employers … prohibited from inquiring into an applicant’s conviction history on an initial employment application until an applicant has been “selected as a finalist.”
applicants for competitive positions with New York State agencies will not be required to discuss or disclose information about prior convictions until … interviewed
places.note: Policy/press release basis; statute (Correction Law Art. 23-A) covers private too but is not a ban-the-box.

places.quote: prohibiting state agencies from inquiring about criminal history on employment applications
prohibits public employers—including cities, counties, and agencies—from inquiring about or considering a job applicant’s criminal history until … “selected for an interview.”

places.note: No source found covering the CNMI.

places.citation: Ohio DAS policy HR-29 (June 2015); HB 56 / Ohio Fair Hiring Act (2015, eff. Mar 23 2016)
places.quote: prohibits all public employers, including cities and counties, from including any questions about criminal records on initial applications for employment
directing all state agencies to remove questions regarding convictions and criminal history from job applications
prohibits an employer from inquiring about an applicant’s prior criminal convictions until the initial interview with the applicant

places.citation: Admin. Policy HR-TM001 (Gov. Wolf, May 5 2017, eff. July 1 2017); Civil Service Commission to match
places.quote: removing questions about conviction history from job applications
Puerto Rico has no laws restricting consideration of criminal record in employment and licensing
prohibits an employer from inquiring about an applicant's prior criminal convictions until the first interview with the applicant
South Carolina has no laws restricting how a criminal record may be considered in the employment context, including no limits on application-stage inquiries.
South Dakota has no laws restricting consideration of criminal record in employment, including limits on application-stage employer inquiries.
prohibits state agencies from inquiring about criminal records on any initial application form
Texas has no laws restricting consideration of criminal record in employment, including limits on application-stage employer inquiries.
prohibits public employers from requiring an applicant to disclose conviction history before an initial interview or, if no interview is conducted, before a conditional job offer
eliminated all criminal records inquiries from applications for state employment
Most public nor private employers may not ask about or consider non-conviction or sealed records.
places.note: Only non-conviction/sealed records addressed; no ban-the-box source found. Left NOT FOUND rather than guessing.

places.quote: requires state agencies and localities to delay inquiries about arrests, charges, and convictions until an interview of the prospective employee

places.citation: HB 1298, Fair Chance Act (2018), RCW 49.94, eff. June 7 2018
places.quote: banning the box for both public- and private-sector employment across Washington
West Virginia has no laws restricting consideration of criminal record in employment, including limits on application-stage employer inquiries.

places.citation: 2015 Wis. Act 150 (AB 373), signed Feb 12 2016, eff. July 1 2016
places.quote: precludes the state from inquiring about a person’s record on the job application and delays inquiries until the applicant is certified for the position
Wyoming has no laws restricting consideration of criminal record in employment, including limits on application-stage employer inquiries.

sources.what: NELP, Ban the Box: Fair Chance State and Local Guide, Oct 2021 (37 states + DC; per-state citations and quotes). Snapshot Oct 2021; changes Nov 2021-Jan 2025 not independently verified.

Collateral Consequences Resource Center 50-state comparison of criminal records in licensing and employment (current version, mentions 2025 laws); source for no-law states, PR, VI, and cross-check of yes states.
NELP web page restating the 37-state list.
Wikipedia pointer only; no state-level details used.

caveats: Nov 2021 to Jan 2025 state changes were not found in a dated source; CCRC (2025 text) shows no new public ban-the-box states and Alabama's 2025 law is licensing only.
New Hampshire sources conflict (NELP yes, CCRC says no application-stage limit).
Arkansas, Iowa 'no' rests on omission from NELP's list plus CCRC's silence on application-stage rules.
Several states' bans are executive orders/policies (AZ, GA, IN, KS, KY, MI, MO, NY, NC, OK, PA, VT, VA partly) and reversible by a new governor.
